requirements.quote:
HTTP/2 servers MUST NOT send post-handshake TLS 1.3
   CertificateRequest messages.  HTTP/2 clients MUST treat a TLS post-
   handshake CertificateRequest message as a connection error
   (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: An HTTP/2 connection is using TLS 1.3 after the handshake.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not send a post-handshake CertificateRequest message.
requirements.why_checkable: A trace of TLS messages sent by an HTTP/2 server can be checked for a CertificateRequest after handshake completion.

requirements.quote:
HTTP/2 servers MUST NOT send post-handshake TLS 1.3
   CertificateRequest messages.  HTTP/2 clients MUST treat a TLS post-
   handshake CertificateRequest message as a connection error
   (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: An HTTP/2 client receives a post-handshake TLS CertificateRequest message.
requirements.error_behavior: The client must treat the message as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A client can be sent a post-handshake CertificateRequest and its resulting connection-level error and error code can be observed.

requirements.quote:
The prohibition on post-handshake authentication applies even if the
   client offered the "post_handshake_auth" TLS extension.  Post-
   handshake authentication support might be advertised independently of
   ALPN [TLS-ALPN].  Clients might offer the capability for use in other
   protocols, but inclusion of the extension cannot imply support within
   HTTP/2.
requirements.condition: The client offered the TLS "post_handshake_auth" extension on an HTTP/2 connection.
requirements.required_behavior: The prohibition on post-handshake authentication must continue to apply.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not interpret inclusion of the extension as support for post-handshake authentication within HTTP/2.
requirements.why_checkable: Negotiation state can be inspected to verify that offering the extension does not enable post-handshake authentication for HTTP/2.

requirements.quote:
TLS early data MAY be used to send requests, provided that the
   guidance in [RFC8470] is observed.  Clients send requests in early
   data assuming initial values for all server settings.
requirements.condition: A client sends HTTP/2 requests using TLS early data.
requirements.required_behavior: The client must observe the guidance in RFC8470 and construct the early-data requests assuming initial values for all server settings.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not base early-data requests on non-initial server setting values.
requirements.why_checkable: Early-data request construction and the setting values assumed before current server settings are received can be inspected in an implementation or test trace.

requirements.quote:
HPACK permits encoding of field names and values that might be
   treated as delimiters in other HTTP versions.  An intermediary that
   translates an HTTP/2 request or response MUST validate fields
   according to the rules in Section 8.2 before translating a message to
   another HTTP version.  Translating a field that includes invalid
   delimiters could be used to cause recipients to incorrectly interpret
   a message, which could be exploited by an attacker.
requirements.condition: An intermediary translates an HTTP/2 request or response into another HTTP version.
requirements.required_behavior: The intermediary must validate the fields according to Section 8.2 before performing the translation.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The intermediary must not translate the message before the required field validation.
requirements.why_checkable: Instrumentation or focused tests can verify that Section 8.2 field validation precedes cross-version translation.

requirements.quote:
Section 8.2 does not include specific rules for validation of pseudo-
   header fields.  If the values of these fields are used, additional
   validation is necessary.  This is particularly important where
   ":scheme", ":authority", and ":path" are combined to form a single
   URI string [RFC3986].  Similar problems might occur when that URI or
   just ":path" is combined with ":method" to construct a request line
   (as in Section 3 of [HTTP/1.1]).  Simple concatenation is not secure
   unless the input values are fully validated.
requirements.condition: An intermediary uses pseudo-header field values, including when combining them into a URI or request line.
requirements.required_behavior: The intermediary must additionally and fully validate the input pseudo-header field values before concatenating them.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The intermediary must not rely on simple concatenation of pseudo-header values that have not been fully validated.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can supply malicious delimiter-bearing pseudo-header values and verify that URI or request-line construction occurs only after additional full validation.

requirements.quote:
An intermediary that receives any fields that require removal before
   forwarding (see Section 7.6.1 of [HTTP]) MUST remove or replace those
   header fields when forwarding messages.  Additionally, intermediaries
   should take care when forwarding messages containing Content-Length
   fields to ensure that the message is well-formed (Section 8.1.1).
   This ensures that if the message is translated into HTTP/1.1 at any
   point, the framing will be correct.
requirements.condition: An intermediary forwards a message containing fields that Section 7.6.1 of HTTP requires to be removed before forwarding.
requirements.required_behavior: The intermediary must remove or replace those header fields when forwarding the message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The intermediary must not forward such fields unchanged.
requirements.why_checkable: A forwarding test can insert a field designated for removal and inspect whether the outgoing message removes or replaces it.

requirements.quote:
An intermediary that receives any fields that require removal before
   forwarding (see Section 7.6.1 of [HTTP]) MUST remove or replace those
   header fields when forwarding messages.  Additionally, intermediaries
   should take care when forwarding messages containing Content-Length
   fields to ensure that the message is well-formed (Section 8.1.1).
   This ensures that if the message is translated into HTTP/1.1 at any
   point, the framing will be correct.
requirements.condition: An intermediary forwards a message containing Content-Length fields.
requirements.required_behavior: The intermediary should ensure that the message is well-formed according to Section 8.1.1 so that translation into HTTP/1.1 produces correct framing.
requirements.why_checkable: Messages with Content-Length fields can be forwarded or translated and checked for the well-formedness and framing properties referenced by the text.
